gloss: spoil, ruin, destroy; corrupt, act corruptly; (שַׁחַת) the pit, corruption
summary: To spoil a thing so that it is no longer good for its use, and so to ruin or destroy it: a loincloth rotted in the ground, a pot marred in the potter's hand, a land laid waste, a city, a people, all flesh in the flood. Of conduct it is to corrupt: all flesh “corrupted its way” and the earth was corrupt (Gen 6:11–12), and Israel “corrupted themselves” with the golden calf (Exo 32:7). The same verb tells the sin and the judgment on it: what had corrupted itself God destroyed. מַשְׁחִית is the destroyer, at Passover and at the threshing floor an angel sent by God and stopped at his word; שַׁחַת is the pit, and the grave where the body decays, which the New Testament reads as “corruption”: David saw it, and the one God raised did not (Act 13:35–37). Arabic saḥata “destroy utterly” and the Aramaic and Phoenician verb share the sense; in the Peshitta it is rust (Jas 5:3).

words.gloss: be spoiled, be corrupt; spoil, ruin, destroy; act corruptly
words.summary: About 150 times, in the piel and hiphil above all, with a few niphal and hophal forms (no qal). Its core is spoiling: what is שָׁחַת is no longer fit for its use (the loincloth “good for nothing”, Jer 13:7), and what is spoiled is destroyed. A people's way or deeds can be spoiled too, and that is corruption, which in Genesis 6 is filled with violence and brings the flood. Its opposite is sparing: “do not destroy it, for a blessing is in it” (Isa 65:8), and Yahweh, being merciful, “did not destroy” (Psa 78:38).

stems.gloss: be spoiled, be ruined; be corrupt

senses.definition: Of a thing or a land: to be marred so that it is no longer good for its use.

evidence.note: The loincloth hidden by the Euphrates: “behold, נִשְׁחַת הָאֵזוֹר, it was good for nothing.”
“The vessel he was making of clay נִשְׁחַת in the hand of the potter, and he made it again another vessel.”
“The land was ruined (תִּשָּׁחֵת) because of the swarm.”

senses.definition: Of the earth or of deeds: to be morally spoiled, filled with violence and evil.

evidence.note: “The earth was corrupt (וַתִּשָּׁחֵת) before God, and the earth was filled with violence (חָמָס).”
“God saw the earth, and behold, it was corrupt (נִשְׁחָתָה), for all flesh had corrupted (הִשְׁחִית) its way on the earth.”
“Not according to your evil ways nor according to your corrupt deeds (עֲלִילוֹתֵיכֶם הַנִּשְׁחָתוֹת).”

stems.gloss: spoil, ruin, destroy; corrupt, act corruptly

senses.definition: To bring to ruin a city, a land, a people or all flesh; to batter down walls; to ravage vines and crops.

evidence.note: “I am bringing the flood of waters on the earth לְשַׁחֵת all flesh in which is the breath of life from under the heavens; all that is on the earth shall expire.”
“Never again shall all flesh be cut off by the waters of the flood, and never again shall there be a flood לְשַׁחֵת the earth.”
“When God destroyed (בְּשַׁחֵת) the cities of the plain … when he overthrew (בַּהֲפֹךְ) the cities”: parallel הָפַךְ.
“Before Yahweh destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.”
“Yahweh has sent us לְשַׁחֲתָהּ.”
“They shall destroy (וְשִׁחֲתוּ) the walls of Tyre and break down her towers.”
Midian came “like locusts … into the land לְשַׁחֲתָהּ”.
“Many shepherds have ruined my vineyard, they have trampled my portion.”
“Go up on her terraces and destroy, but make not a full end.”
“He has destroyed his strongholds.”
“He has destroyed his place of meeting.”
Saul seeks to come to Keilah “to destroy the city on my account”.
“How were you not afraid to put forth your hand to destroy the anointed of Yahweh?”
“That the avenger of blood destroy no more, and they not destroy my son.”
“You will destroy all this people.”
“The nations which my fathers destroyed.”
“You have destroyed your land, you have slain your people.”
“My eye spared them from destroying them, and I did not make an end of them in the wilderness.”
“I sought a man … to stand in the breach before me for the land, that I should not destroy it.”
“I will not return to destroy Ephraim, for I am God and not man.”
“It has destroyed you, Israel, that you are against me, your help.”

senses.definition: To spoil a thing so that it is lost to its use: seed spilled on the ground, an eye put out, pleasant words wasted, compassion stifled.

evidence.note: Onan “וְשִׁחֵת on the ground, so as not to give seed to his brother”: wasted it.
“If a man strikes the eye of his servant … וְשִׁחֲתָהּ, he shall let him go free for his eye.”
“The morsel you have eaten you will vomit up, and waste your pleasant words.”
Edom pursued his brother with the sword “וְשִׁחֵת רַחֲמָיו”: stifled his compassion.

senses.definition: To spoil one's own way, wisdom or a covenant: to turn aside from the way Yahweh commanded, above all to idols.

evidence.note: “Go down, for your people whom you brought up from the land of Egypt שִׁחֵת”: the golden calf (32:8).
“Your people שִׁחֵת; they have turned aside quickly from the way which I commanded them; they have made themselves a molten image.”
“They have corrupted themselves toward him; they are not his sons, it is their blemish (מוּמָם), a perverse and crooked generation.”
“You have turned aside from the way, you have caused many to stumble in the law, שִׁחַתֶּם the covenant of Levi.”
“Your heart was lifted up because of your beauty; you corrupted your wisdom because of your splendour.”
“They have deeply corrupted themselves, as in the days of Gibeah.”

senses.definition: To destroy a city, a land, a people or a kingdom; often of Yahweh's judgment, and of his mercy in not destroying.

evidence.note: “The end of all flesh has come before me, for the earth is filled with violence through them; behold, I will destroy them (מַשְׁחִיתָם) with the earth”: the verb of their corruption (6:12).
“Will you destroy all the city for lack of five? … I will not destroy it if I find forty-five there.”
“We are destroying this place.”
“Get out of this place, for Yahweh is destroying the city.”
“As when new wine is found in the cluster and one says, Do not destroy it, for a blessing is in it, so I will do for my servants' sake, not to destroy them all.”
Moses: “Lord Yahweh, do not destroy your people and your inheritance which you redeemed.”
“Yahweh would not destroy you.”
“Yahweh your God is a merciful God (אֵל רַחוּם); he will not fail you nor destroy you nor forget the covenant of your fathers.”
“But he, being merciful, atoned for iniquity and did not destroy.”
“He said he would annihilate them (לְהַשְׁמִידָם), had not Moses his chosen stood in the breach before him to turn his wrath from destroying.”
“Yahweh would not destroy Judah for David his servant's sake.”
Rabshakeh: “Have I come up against this place to destroy it without Yahweh?”
In the kingdom: “They shall not hurt (יָרֵעוּ) nor destroy in all my holy mountain, for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of Yahweh.”
“The king of Babylon shall come and destroy this land and cause to cease from it man and beast.”
“His purpose is against Babylon to destroy it, for it is the vengeance of Yahweh.”
“With you I shatter nations, with you I destroy kingdoms.”
“Yahweh purposed to destroy the wall of the daughter of Zion.”
They burned the house of God, broke down the wall of Jerusalem “and destroyed all its precious vessels”.
“After the sixty-two sevens the anointed one shall be cut off … and the people of the prince who is to come shall destroy (יַשְׁחִית) the city and the sanctuary.”
“He shall destroy wonderfully … and destroy the mighty and the people of the holy ones.”
“God sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it, and as he was destroying, Yahweh saw and relented.”
David to Abishai of Saul: “Do not destroy him; for who can put forth his hand against the anointed of Yahweh and be guiltless?”
“They ravaged the sons of Ammon and besieged Rabbah.”
“All the people with Joab were battering the wall to throw it down.”
In a siege “you shall not destroy its trees by wielding an axe against them, for you may eat of them, and you shall not cut them down (תִכְרֹת)”.
“They destroyed the produce of the land.”
“I will rebuke the devourer for you, and he shall not destroy the fruit of your ground.”
“Your mice that ravage the land.”
“Let us destroy the tree with its fruit and cut him off from the land of the living.”
“So will I ruin the pride of Judah”: the spoiled loincloth of 13:7 made the sign.
“Ah, Lord Yahweh! Will you destroy all the remnant of Israel?”
“The anger of Yahweh turned from him, not to destroy him completely.”

senses.gloss: mar, damage, ruin (a thing, one's life)
senses.definition: To spoil a thing short of destroying it: the corners of the beard, an inheritance; to ruin one's own life or a neighbour.

evidence.note: “You shall not round the corners of your head, nor mar (תַשְׁחִית) the corners of your beard.”
The near kinsman: “I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I mar my own inheritance.”
“He who commits adultery … he who does it destroys his own soul (מַשְׁחִית נַפְשׁוֹ).”
“With his mouth the godless destroys his neighbour.”

senses.definition: To spoil one's way or deeds: to turn aside from the way Yahweh commanded, to idols, abominations and evil; with no object, to act corruptly.

evidence.note: “All flesh had corrupted its way (הִשְׁחִית … אֶת־דַּרְכּוֹ) on the earth.”
“Lest you act corruptly and make yourselves a carved image.”
“After my death you will utterly corrupt yourselves and turn aside from the way which I have commanded you.”
When the judge died “they turned back and acted more corruptly than their fathers, in following other gods”.
“The fool says in his heart, No God. They are corrupt (הִשְׁחִיתוּ), they do abominable (הִתְעִיבוּ) deeds; there is none who does good.”
“Seed of evildoers, sons who deal corruptly (בָּנִים מַשְׁחִיתִים); they have forsaken Yahweh.”
“They are bronze and iron; they all deal corruptly.”
“You were more corrupt than they in all your ways.”
“But they rose early and corrupted all their deeds.”
Uzziah: “his heart was lifted up to his destruction (or: so that he acted corruptly), and he transgressed against Yahweh.”
“And the people still acted corruptly.”

senses.definition: The participle מָשְׁחָת: an animal with a blemish, unfit for offering; a fountain fouled.

evidence.note: “Cursed be the deceiver who has a male in his flock and vows it, and sacrifices to the Lord a blemished thing (מָשְׁחָת).”
“A trampled spring and a spoiled fountain (מָקוֹר מָשְׁחָת) is a righteous man who gives way before the wicked.”

evidence.locator: Jer.51.25, הַמַּשְׁחִית אֶת־כָּל־הָאָרֶץ → τὸ διαφθεῖρον πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν; διαφθείρω renders שָׁחַת ×42

evidence.note: “To destroy (διαφθεῖραι) those who destroy (τοὺς διαφθείροντας) the earth”: the words of Jer 51:25 for Babylon, “the destroyer of all the earth”; the Peshitta has ܚܒܠ for both.
“Men corrupted (διεφθαρμένων) in mind”: the moral sense, as Gen 6:12.

evidence.locator: Gen.6.12, נִשְׁחָתָה → κατεφθαρμένη, הִשְׁחִית → κατέφθειρεν; Gen.6.13, מַשְׁחִיתָם → καταφθείρω; Gen.6.17 and 9.11, לְשַׁחֵת → καταφθεῖραι

evidence.note: “Men corrupted (κατεφθαρμένοι) in mind, reprobate concerning the faith.”
“They shall utterly perish (καταφθαρήσονται) in their own corruption.”

evidence.locator: Gen.6.11, וַתִּשָּׁחֵת הָאָרֶץ → ἐφθάρη ἡ γῆ

evidence.note: The great harlot “who corrupted (ἔφθειρε) the earth with her fornication”: the corrupted earth of Gen 6:11 and the destroyer of the earth of Jer 51:25.

parallels.note: turn aside from the way: the corrupting of oneself.
violence, which fills the corrupted earth.

opposites.note: merciful: Yahweh's mercy is that he does not destroy.

phrases.gloss: do not destroy: Moses' plea, and the heading of four psalms

words.summary: The hiphil participle used as a noun: one who destroys, whether an angel sent by God, an army of raiders, a lion, a wind or a nation; and, with לְ, destruction itself. BDB's tokens overlap the verb's hiphil participles; both are counted.

senses.definition: One who destroys: the angel sent against Egypt and against Jerusalem, raiders, a lion, Babylon; created and sent by Yahweh.

evidence.note: “Yahweh will pass through to strike the Egyptians … Yahweh will pass over the door and will not allow the destroyer (הַמַּשְׁחִית) to come into your houses to strike”; in 12:13 it is “my striking”.
“Yahweh said to the angel, the destroyer among the people (לַמַּלְאָךְ הַמַּשְׁחִית בָּעָם), Enough; now stay your hand.”
“God sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it … and said to the destroying angel, Enough.”
“The angel of Yahweh destroying in all the borders of Israel.”
“I have created the smith … and I have created the destroyer to destroy (מַשְׁחִית לְחַבֵּל).”
“A lion has gone up from his thicket, and a destroyer of nations (מַשְׁחִית גּוֹיִם) has set out.”
“Your sword has devoured your prophets like a destroying lion.”
“I will prepare destroyers against you, each with his weapons.”
“A destroying wind” against Babylon.
“Behold, I am against you, mountain of the destroyer (הַר הַמַּשְׁחִית), who destroys all the earth.”
“The raiders (הַמַּשְׁחִית) came out of the camp of the Philistines in three companies.”
The high places “on the right of the mount of the destroyer (הַר־הַמַּשְׁחִית)”, east of Jerusalem, built by Solomon for Ashtoreth, Chemosh and Milcom.
“He who is slack in his work is brother to the master of destruction (בַּעַל מַשְׁחִית).”
“He who robs his father or mother and says, It is no transgression, is companion to a man who destroys.”
Of fowlers: “they set a trap (מַשְׁחִית), they catch men”: the destroying snare.

senses.definition: With לְ: for, to destruction; the ruin that comes on a man or a people.

evidence.note: “When I see the blood I will pass over you, and there shall be no plague on you for destruction (לְמַשְׁחִית) when I strike the land of Egypt.”
“No strength remained in me, and my splendour was turned in me to ruin (לְמַשְׁחִית).”
“Slay to destruction old and young … but do not come near any man on whom is the mark.”
“The evil arrows of famine, which shall be for destruction.”
“Brutish men, skilful to destroy (חָרָשֵׁי מַשְׁחִית).”
Ammon and Moab “helped each to destroy the other”.
The house of Ahab “were his counsellors after his father's death, to his destruction”.
“By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood, lest he who destroyed (ὁ ὀλοθρεύων) the firstborn should touch them”: Exo 12:23.
“Do not murmur, as some of them murmured and were destroyed by the destroyer (ὑπὸ τοῦ ὀλοθρευτοῦ)”: the plague of Num 16:41–49; the Peshitta has ܡܚܒܠܢܐ.

parallels.note: lion, the image of the destroyer of nations.

phrases.gloss: mount of the destroyer: the hill of Solomon's idol shrines; Babylon

words.gloss: pit; the pit of death, corruption
words.summary: A pit dug as a trap, and the pit of death where the body lies and decays. 23 times, in the Psalms, Job and the prophets. BDB files it under שׁוח “sink down”, with שׁוּחָה and שִׁיחָה, also dug pits (Jer 18:20; Psa 57:7), and the trap uses match theirs; but the New Testament, expounding Psa 16:10, reads it as “corruption” (διαφθορά, Peshitta ܚܒܠܐ): David “saw corruption”, the one God raised did not (Act 13:35–37), and Job calls it his father beside the worm his mother (Job 17:14). The entry keeps it here for that reading; which root it is formed from is open.

senses.definition: A pit dug and covered to catch a man or a beast, often with a net; the wicked fall into the pit they dug.

evidence.note: “He made a pit (בּוֹר) and dug it, and has fallen into the שַׁחַת he made.”
“The nations have sunk into the pit they made; in the net which they hid their own foot is caught.”
“Without cause they hid for me their net, a pit; without cause they dug for my soul.”
“Until a pit is dug for the wicked.”
“Whoever digs a pit will fall into it.”
The young lion “was caught in their pit”.
“They spread their net over him; he was caught in their pit.”
“You would plunge me into the pit, and my own clothes would abhor me”: a filthy ditch.

senses.definition: The pit the dead go down to, the grave where the body decays; to “see the pit” is to die and decay, and to be redeemed from it is to be kept alive or raised. The New Testament reads it as corruption, decay.

evidence.note: “You will not abandon my soul to the grave (לִשְׁאוֹל), nor let your faithful one see שָׁחַת.”
Peter quoting Psa 16:10: “nor let your Holy One see corruption (διαφθοράν; Peshitta ܚܒܠܐ).”
“He spoke of the resurrection of the Christ, that his soul was not left in the grave, nor did his flesh see corruption.”
“David … fell asleep and was laid with his fathers and saw corruption; but he whom God raised saw no corruption.”
“I have said to the pit, You are my father; to the worm (לָרִמָּה), My mother and my sister.”
“That he should live on for ever and not see the pit”: no ransom buys that (49:8–9).
“What profit is in my blood when I go down to the pit? Will the dust praise you?”
“You have loved my soul out of the pit of corruption (מִשַּׁחַת בְּלִי) … for the grave cannot thank you” (38:18).
“He keeps back his soul from the pit and his life from perishing by the sword.”
“His soul draws near to the pit, and his life to the destroyers.”
“Deliver him from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom (כֹּפֶר).”
“He has redeemed my soul from going down to the pit, and my life shall see the light.”
“Who redeems your life from the pit.”
“You brought up my life from the pit, Yahweh my God.”
“He shall not die and go down to the pit.”
“They shall bring you down to the pit, and you shall die the death of the slain.”
“You will bring them down to the well of the pit (לִבְאֵר שַׁחַת); men of blood shall not live out half their days.”

evidence.locator: Psa.16.10, Psa.30.10, Job.33.28, שַׁחַת → διαφθοράν; Psa.49.10 → καταφθοράν; διαφθορά renders שַׁחַת ×7

evidence.note: Quoting Psa 16:10.
“No more to return to corruption … David saw corruption, but he whom God raised saw no corruption.”

parallels.note: worm: the decay of the body.

phrases.gloss: see the pit, see corruption: die and decay
go down to the pit: die

words.summary: Once, in כְּלִי מַשְׁחֵתוֹ “his weapon of destroying”, the weapon of each of the six executioners sent through Jerusalem.

senses.definition: Destroying, in “the weapon of his destroying”.

evidence.note: “Draw near, you who have charge over the city, each with his weapon of destroying (כְּלִי מַשְׁחֵתוֹ) in his hand.”
What they were sent to do: “slay to destruction (לְמַשְׁחִית)”.

words.summary: Once, of the servant of Yahweh whose appearance was marred beyond any man's. The word's tokens in the count are inflated: BDB's key shares its spelling with מִשְׁחָה “anointing”, so the anointing oil's verses are counted too; only Isa 52:14 is this word.

senses.definition: The marring of a man's appearance, so that he no longer looks like a man.

evidence.note: “As many were astonished at you, so marred (מִשְׁחַת) beyond any man was his appearance, and his form beyond the sons of man.”

words.summary: Once, of animals bruised, crushed, torn or cut (Lev 22:24), unfit to offer. As with מִשְׁחַת, BDB's key shares its tokens with מִשְׁחָה “anointing”; only Lev 22:25 is this word.

senses.definition: The spoiling of an animal's body that makes it unfit for an offering, set beside מוּם “blemish”.

evidence.note: “You shall not offer any of these as the bread of your God from a foreigner's hand, for their corruption (מָשְׁחָתָם) is in them, a blemish (מוּם) is in them; they shall not be accepted for you.”
What “these” are: bruised, crushed, torn or cut.

words.gloss: (passive participle) corrupt; a corrupt thing, fault
words.summary: Biblical Aramaic, only as the feminine passive participle שְׁחִיתָה used as a noun: a corrupt word, a fault in conduct.

senses.definition: Of words, lying and corrupt; of an official's conduct, a fault or corruption, set beside negligence and opposed to faithfulness.

evidence.note: Nebuchadnezzar: “you have agreed to speak lying and corrupt words (מִלָּה כִדְבָה וּשְׁחִיתָה) before me.”
“They could find no occasion or fault (וּשְׁחִיתָה), because he was faithful (מְהֵימַן), and no negligence (שָׁלוּ) or fault was found in him.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܫܚܬ (šḥet), once, of gold and silver that have rusted: the metal spoiled and eaten away.

senses.definition: Of precious metal hoarded: to rust, tarnish, be eaten away.

evidence.note: “Your gold and your silver have rusted (אַשְׁחֵת), and their rust will be a witness against you and will eat your flesh like fire.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܫܘܚܬܐ (šuḥtā), rust, for the Greek ἰός in Jas 5:3.

senses.definition: The rust or tarnish on metal, the sign of its decay.

evidence.note: “Their rust (וְשׁוּחְתְּהוֹן) will be a witness against you.”

cognates.gloss: extirpate, destroy utterly, do away with; shave or peel off entirely; (suḥt) unlawful, foul gain, a bribe
cognates.note: The Hebrew's destroying, and its marring of the beard (Lev 19:27) in the shaving off of hair; suḥt, gain that is forbidden and foul, a bribe to a judge, is the corruption of conduct. Arabic s answers to Hebrew š, and ḥ (not ḫ) stands behind ח.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1314, art. سحت, سَحَتَهُ (n19044)
evidence.note: “He extirpated it, eradicated it, exterminated it, or destroyed it utterly … made an end of it … He shaved his head so as to remove the hair utterly … He peeled off the fat from the flesh.” In Kur xx. 64, “lest He destroy you by a punishment”.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1314, art. سحت, سُحْتٌ (n19046)
evidence.note: “A thing that is forbidden, prohibited, or unlawful … what is disapproved, abominable, or foul, of gains … a bribe that is given to a judge.”

cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic, in the Targums: the same verb as the Hebrew. The Targum of Lev 22:24 calls the bruised, crushed or cut animal שְׁחִית “mutilated”, the very animals Lev 22:25 says have מָשְׁחָת in them. Aramaic keeps š apart from ṯ (which it writes ת), so שׁ shows š.

evidence.locator: s.v. שְׁחַת (ch.), “same” (as Hebrew שָׁחַת); part. pass. שְׁחִית mutilated, Targ. Y. Lev. XXII, 24

cognates.gloss: decay, rust; corrupt, ruin, destroy, smash
cognates.note: Phoenician has both sides of the root: the decay and rust of the Peshitta's ܫܚܬ, and destroying. Phoenician writes ḥ and ḫ alike, so it shows no sound behind ח.

evidence.note: “to decay, rust; to corrupt, ruin, destroy, smash”; compares Hebrew שִׁחֵת, Aramaic שְׁחַת and Syriac ܫܚܬ.

cognates.note: The corrosion on copper, as the Peshitta's ܫܘܚܬܐ is rust. Akkadian ḫ usually answers to an older ḫ, not the ḥ the Arabic shows, so it may be a loan or a separate word; no sound is recorded.

evidence.note: “patina”.

doctrine.statement: Genesis tells the flood in this one verb. “The earth was corrupt (וַתִּשָּׁחֵת) before God … for all flesh had corrupted (הִשְׁחִית) its way on the earth”, and God said, “behold, I will destroy them (מַשְׁחִיתָם) with the earth” (Gen 6:11–13): what had corrupted itself he destroyed. The flood came “to destroy all flesh in which is the breath of life, from under the heavens; all that is on the earth shall expire” (Gen 6:17), and afterwards God covenanted that “never again shall there be a flood to destroy the earth … to destroy all flesh” (Gen 9:11, 15). The promise is kept only if that flood destroyed all flesh under the whole heavens, for local floods have come since; it was a flood over all the earth, and Peter says “the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished” (2Pe 3:6).

To die is to go down to שַׁחַת and see it: “what profit is in my blood when I go down to the pit? Will the dust praise you?” (Psa 30:10); no man can “live on for ever and not see the pit” (Psa 49:10); Job calls the pit his father and the worm his mother (Job 17:14). Peter and Paul read the word as corruption, decay: David “fell asleep, was laid with his fathers and saw corruption” (Act 13:36), and “David did not ascend into the heavens” (Act 2:34). The dead man is in the grave, decaying, not living elsewhere; the only way out of the pit the verses give is God's redeeming and raising (Psa 103:4; Job 33:24, 28).

“You will not abandon my soul to the grave, nor let your faithful one see שָׁחַת” (Psa 16:10). Peter says David spoke it of the resurrection of the Christ, “that his soul was not left in the grave, nor did his flesh see corruption”, for “this Jesus God raised up” (Act 2:27–32); Paul, that God raised him “no more to return to corruption … he whom God raised saw no corruption” (Act 13:34–37). Jesus died and was buried, and God raised him on the third day before his body decayed; it is his resurrection, not a soul surviving death, that the psalm foretold.

The destroyer (הַמַּשְׁחִית) at the Passover is Yahweh's own agent: “Yahweh will pass through to strike the Egyptians … and will not allow the destroyer to come into your houses” (Exo 12:23), which he calls “my striking” (Exo 12:13). At the threshing floor “God sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it”, and Yahweh “said to the angel, the destroyer, Enough; stay your hand” (1Ch 21:15; 2Sa 24:16). “I have created the destroyer to destroy” (Isa 54:16). The destroying angel is sent by God, does his will and stops at his word; the verses know no destroyer acting against God, and Hebrews counts it the destroyer of the firstborn whom faith in the Passover blood kept away (Heb 11:28).

Daniel was told that after the sixty-two sevens “the anointed one shall be cut off … and the people of the prince who is to come shall destroy (יַשְׁחִית) the city and the sanctuary, and its end shall be with a flood” (Dan 9:26). Messiah was cut off, and a generation later the Roman armies under Titus destroyed Jerusalem and the temple in AD 70, as Jesus foretold: “when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, know that its desolation has come near … Jerusalem shall be trodden down by the nations” (Luk 21:20, 24), “there shall not be left here one stone upon another” (Mat 24:2).

They want their own entry (שטה/שנט); not followed here. If a שׁוח entry is written, decide whether the trap sense goes there and the corruption sense stays, or one word in one place. (4) Psa 57:1, 58:1, 59:1, 75:1 headings אַל־תַּשְׁחֵת are in the verb's token list but cited only under the phrase.
